did: Made the investigative essay "Everything is slow: our code, or the hardware?" entirely in this session, 11:30 in the cheat-sheet series, version 7. It has the intro and outro, music bed, legend, freshness rule, and a stamp at server@fceea07 and some-ui@72346fa, and cards-check passes it. It runs on SLOW-PROBE's v4 hypothesis and rule. The null, that the hardware sets the time, is rejected, and the $600 card recommends no purchase. Chapter one is the owner's own spoken abstract: cut at word boundaries, 1.15x tempo, transcribed by whisper here, never through home. Tin Bird and Mochi host it as a separate, deterministic layer drawn over the finished video by the HOST prototype's rig. It shows framing, expressions, pointing on spoken words, blinks, and Mochi celebrating the verdict. Delivered on a private page with the video, thumbnail, description and cut list. The 55 MB master is in Drive's Inbox, uploaded as the service account with the owner's direct permission, and its md5 matches.

calls.title: The owner's abstract plays as a card scene's narration, carried by Mochi (C1504)
options: seed the owner's take into the recorder's step cache as the scene's narration
a spoken card, which adds the tin sparrow and claims home heard the take
splice the take in after rendering, with captions drawn separately
calls.why: The pipeline's own captions, chapters and music bed then apply, and there are only two characters on screen. The cut list stays off testing, so home never renders a Kokoro reading of the owner's words.
calls.undo: Render the cut list without the seeded cache, and Kokoro reads the abstract. Or make the scene a spoken card once home holds the take.

add testing@c95c283 to the stamp too

left: The master in Drive's Inbox is a one-off. The owner trashes it once the video is on YouTube.
The service account drive-reader got writer on the folder Inbox/everything-is-slow-2026-11-24 only, for this upload. Remove that share, or trash the folder, once the video is up.
The host layer's pointing targets are hand-set frame pixels, a corner host can overlap a two-column card, and whether the host moves into the renderer is open. All three are on HOST #3521.
The abstract runs 2:14, over the 2:00 aim, because every one of the owner's words was kept.
